American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Dubai Basketball]] of the [[ABA League]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia Cavaliers]] before being selected with the 21st overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]] by the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|title=MAVS SELECT JUSTIN ANDERSON 21ST, SATNAM SINGH 52ND IN NBA DRAFT|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavs-2015-draft-picks/|work=Mavs.com|date=June 25, 2015|access-date=June 27, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150627144749/http://www.mavs.com/mavs-2015-draft-picks/|archive-date=June 27, 2015|url-status=dead}}{{cite magazine|title=Mavericks select Justin Anderson with No. 21 pick in 2015 NBA draft|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2015/06/25/justin-anderson-2015-nba-draft-dallas-mavericks|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=June 25, 2015|access-date=June 25, 2015}} ==High school career== Anderson attended [[Montrose Christian School]] where he averaged 17.8 points, 4.7 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 1.8 steals and 1.6 blocks per game as a senior and won several awards, among them, the Gatorade Maryland Boys Basketball Player of the Year. He was a Top 100 Recruit by [[ESPN]] and [[Rivals.com]].{{cite web|url=http://www.virginiasports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/justin_anderson_809102.html|title=Justin Anderson espn overall = 49 | 247 overall = 51 | accessdate = 2015-03-30 | bball = yes }} ==College career== [[File:Justin Anderson Virginia.jpg|thumb|left|Anderson with [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]] in 2014|265x265px]] Anderson originally verbally committed to [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]], but later changed his commitment following [[Gary Williams]]’ retirement.{{cite web|title=Patience, practice propelled Justin Anderson to starring role at Virginia|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2015/01/14/justin-anderson-virginia-cavaliers-acc|access-date=March 30, 2015|date=January 14, 2015|publisher=[[Sports Illustrated]]}} On November 12, 2011, Anderson signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play for [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]].{{cite web|title=Four Sign Letters Of Intent With Virginia Men's Basketball|url=http://www.virginiasports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111211aaa.html|work=VirginiaSports.com|access-date=November 12, 2011|date=November 12, 2011}} Anderson primarily played off the bench his first two seasons at Virginia. His play during his sophomore year garnered him [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) [[Sixth Man]] of the Year honors. Following the graduation of [[Joe Harris (basketball)|Joe Harris]], Anderson was inserted into the starting lineup. A fractured finger against [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]] and an appendectomy forced Anderson to miss the last eight games of the regular season, but he returned in time for Virginia's first game of the [[2015 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]]. After putting up career-high numbers in scoring and other offensive categories, Anderson was named second-team All-ACC and third-team All-American by the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]]. On April 13, 2015, Anderson declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his senior year.{{cite web|title=Latest NBA Draft projection for UVa's Justin Anderson|url=http://virginia.247sports.com/Bolt/Latest-NBA-Draft-projection-for-UVas-Justin-Anderson-37711032|work=247sports.com|access-date=June 12, 2015|date=June 11, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150615032424/http://virginia.247sports.com/Bolt/Latest-NBA-Draft-projection-for-UVas-Justin-Anderson-37711032|archive-date=June 15, 2015|url-status=dead}} ==Professional career== ===Dallas Mavericks (2015–2017)=== On June 25, 2015, Anderson was selected by the [[Dallas Mavericks]] with the 21st overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]]. He joined the Mavericks for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]], where he averaged 17.5 points, 4.2 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.2 steals in six games. On August 1, 2015, he signed a 2-year, $3 million rookie scale contract with the Mavericks.{{cite web|title=Mavericks sign first-round pick Justin Anderson|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-first-round-pick-justin-anderson/|date=August 1, 2015|work=Mavs.com|access-date=August 1, 2015}} He made his debut for the Mavericks in their season opener on October 28, 2015, recording two points and one rebound in a 111–95 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|title=8 Dallas players reach double figures, Mavs rout Suns 111-95|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/DALPHX/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2015|access-date=October 28, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160330130800/http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/DALPHX/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 30, 2016|url-status=dead}} On November 10, 2015, he scored a then season-high 11 points on 4-of-4 shooting in a 120–105 loss to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web|title=Davis leaves with injured hip as Pelicans get first win|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151110/DALNOP/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=November 10, 2015|access-date=November 10, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161005163757/http://www.nba.com/games/20151110/DALNOP/gameinfo.html|archive-date=October 5, 2016|url-status=dead}} On February 5, 2016, he set a new season high with 13 points in a 116–90 loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|title=Justin Anderson 2015-16 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/a/anderju01/gamelog/2016/|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=January 22, 2017}} On April 8, 2016, he recorded his first career double-double with 19 points and 10 rebounds (both career highs) in a 103–93 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|title=Mavs beat Grizzlies, close in on playoffs after Barea injury|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160408/MEMDAL/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=April 8, 2016|access-date=April 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190414142428/https://www.nba.com/games/20160408/MEMDAL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 14, 2019|url-status=dead}} During his rookie season, he received multiple assignments to the [[Texas Legends]], the Mavericks' [[NBA Development League|D-League]] affiliate.{{cite web|title=All-Time NBA Assignments|url=http://dleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 22, 2017|archive-date=March 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170322122733/http://dleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|url-status=dead}} In July 2016, Anderson re-joined the Mavericks for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]], where he averaged 16.0 points, 7.0 rebounds and 2.6 assists in five games. On November 9, 2016, he had a season-best game with 16 points, eight rebounds and seven assists in a 116–95 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web|title=Justin Anderson 2016-17 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/a/anderju01/gamelog/2017/|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=January 22, 2017}} On January 22, 2017, he scored a season-high 19 points in a 122–73 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|title=Nowitzki starts Mavericks toward 122-73 rout of Lakers|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900083|work=ESPN.com|date=January 22, 2017|access-date=January 22, 2017}} ===Philadelphia 76ers (2017–2018)=== On February 23, 2017, Anderson was traded, along with [[Andrew Bogut]] and a protected first-round pick, to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in exchange for [[Nerlens Noel]].{{cite web|title=Philadelphia 76ers Acquire First-Round Pick, Justin Anderson, and Andrew Bogut From Dallas|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/nerlens-release-draft|work=NBA.com|date=February 23, 2017|access-date=February 23, 2017}} On March 3, 2017, he made the go-ahead basket with 24.3 seconds left and matched his career high with 19 points in the 76ers' 105–102 victory over the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|title=Anderson, Saric lead 76ers past Knicks, 105-102|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900304|work=ESPN.com|date=March 3, 2017|access-date=March 4, 2017}} Three days later, he had another 19-point effort in a 112–98 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|title=Antetokounmpo, Snell lead Bucks past 76ers, 112-98|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900329|work=ESPN.com|date=March 6, 2017|access-date=March 7, 2017}} On March 17, 2017, he had his fifth career 19-point game (fourth time in 2016–17) in a 116–74 win over his former team, the Dallas Mavericks.{{cite web|title=76ers rout Mavericks in Noel's return to Philadelphia|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900415|work=ESPN.com|date=March 17, 2017|access-date=March 18, 2017}} In the 76ers' season finale on April 12, 2017, Anderson had a 26-point effort in a 114–113 loss to the Knicks.{{cite web|title=Anthony helps Knicks edge 76ers 114-113 in finale|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900598|work=ESPN.com|date=April 12, 2017|access-date=April 13, 2017}} In a win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] on April 11, 2018, Anderson scored a season-high 25 points and had six rebounds.{{cite news|title=76ers' Justin Anderson: Scores season-high 25 points in Wednesday's win|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/76ers-justin-anderson-scores-season-high-25-points-in-wednesdays-win/|work=CBS Sports|date=April 12, 2018|access-date=May 8, 2018}} ===Atlanta Hawks (2018–2019)=== On July 25, 2018, Anderson was traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in a three-team deal involving the 76ers and the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|title=Hawks Complete Three-Team Trade With OKC and 76ers|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-complete-three-team-trade-okc-and-76ers|work=NBA.com|date=July 25, 2018|access-date=July 25, 2018}} On March 31, 2019, he set season highs with 24 points and 12 rebounds in a 136–135 overtime win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|title=Hawks top Bucks in OT on Young buzzer-beater|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071818|work=ESPN.com|date=March 31, 2019|access-date=April 1, 2019}} On June 29, 2019, the Hawks declined Anderson's contract extension, making him an unrestricted free agent.{{cite web|title=Hawks decline to make qualifying offer to Justin Anderson|url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/basketball/hawks-decline-make-qualifying-offer-tojustin-anderson/rv5hjnevD4sZdrv8vGoEOI/|website=AJC.com|date=June 29, 2019|access-date=June 29, 2019}} ===Raptors 905 (2019–2020)=== On September 26, 2019, Anderson signed with the [[Washington Wizards]] for training camp.{{cite web|title=Wizards announce 2019 training camp roster|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-announce-2019-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=September 26, 2019|access-date=September 26, 2019}} On October 16, 2019, Anderson was waived by the Wizards after appearing in the team's four preseason games.{{cite web|title=Wizards waive three players|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-waive-anderson-jones-booth-2019-20|work=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2019|access-date=October 16, 2019}} On November 25, 2019, the [[Raptors 905]] announced that they had claimed Anderson off waivers.{{cite web|title=.@Raptors905 have claimed Justin Anderson from the waiver wire. Anderson played 48 games with the Atlanta Hawks last season. He will wear #8.|url=https://twitter.com/Raptors905MR/status/1199007945327071232|website=Raptors905MR on Twitter.com|date=November 25, 2019|access-date=November 25, 2019}} ===Brooklyn Nets (2020)=== On January 6, 2020, Anderson signed a ten-day contract with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Justin Anderson to 10-day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2020/01/06/brooklyn-nets-sign-justin-anderson-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=January 6, 2020|access-date=January 6, 2020}} On January 15, he was released by the Nets.{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot to 10-day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2020/01/15/brooklyn-nets-sign-timoth-luwawu-cabarrot-to-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=January 16, 2020|access-date=January 16, 2020}} ===Return to the 905 (2020)=== Anderson rejoined the Raptors 905 after the expiration of his 10-day contract with the Nets. ===Long Island Nets (2020)=== On January 21, 2020, the Raptors 905 traded Anderson to the [[Long Island Nets]] in exchange for [[Henry Ellenson]].{{cite web|title=Long Island Nets Acquire Justin Anderson in Trade with Raptors 905|url=https://longisland.gleague.nba.com/news/long-island-nets-acquire-justin-anderson-in-trade-with-raptors-905/|website=gleague.nba.com|date=January 21, 2020|access-date=January 22, 2020}} ===Return to Brooklyn (2020)=== On July 18, 2020, the Nets announced that they had signed Anderson for the remainder of the [[2019–20 NBA season]].{{cite web|title=BROOKLYN NETS SIGN JUSTIN ANDERSON|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2020/07/18/brooklyn-nets-sign-justin-anderson|website=NBA.com|date=July 18, 2020|access-date=July 18, 2020}} On December 3, Anderson signed a partially guaranteed 2-year, $4 million contract to return to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|title=Team Signs Anderson, Walton Jr., and Re-Signs Broekhoff|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/team-signs-anderson-walton-jr-and-re-signs-broekhoff|website=NBA.com|date=December 3, 2020|access-date=December 4, 2020}}{{Cite web |title='Simba' returns as Sixers bring back familiar face |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/sixers/justin-anderson-sixers-contract-nba-training-camp-sixers-roster-isaiah-joe-paul-reed |access-date=March 5, 2022 |website=NBC Sports|date=November 27, 2020 }} He was waived at the conclusion of training camp. ===Cleveland Cavaliers / Fort Wayne Mad Ants (2021)=== On September 23, 2021, the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] acquired the rights to Anderson in a trade with the Long Island Nets.{{cite web|title=Fort Wayne Acquires Justin Anderson's Rights in Trade with Long Island|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/fort-wayne-acquires-justin-andersons-rights-in-trade-with-long-island/n-574917|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=September 23, 2021|access-date=November 7, 2021}} On October 15, Anderson signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the [[Indiana Pacers]]. He was waived the next day and subsequently joined the Mad Ants.{{cite web|title=Justin Anderson: Gets signed, waived by Pacers|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/justin-anderson-gets-signed-waived-by-pacers/|website=CBS Sports|date=October 18, 2021|access-date=March 5, 2022}} In 11 games, he averaged 14.3 points, 6.5 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 1.0 steals in 33.8 minutes per contest.{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Sign Justin Anderson and Luke Kornet|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/player-signings-211221|website=NBA.com|date=December 21, 2021|access-date=December 21, 2021}} On December 21, 2021, Anderson signed a 10-day contract with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. ===Indiana Pacers / Fort Wayne Mad Ants (2022–2023)=== On January 1, 2022, Anderson signed a 10-day contract with the [[Indiana Pacers]]{{cite web|title=Pacers Sign Justin Anderson and Lance Stephenson to 10-Day Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-justin-anderson-and-lance-stephenson-10-day-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=January 1, web|title=Pacers Sign Justin Anderson to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-justin-anderson-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=March 17, 2022|access-date=March 29, the [[Indiana Mad Ants|Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] roster for training camp.{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/mad-ants-announce-2022-training-camp-roster/n-5892665|website=oursportscentral.com|title=Mad Ants Announce 2022 Training Camp Roster|date=October 24, 2022|access-date=October 24, 2022}} ===Río Breogán (2023)=== On October 25, 2023, Anderson signed with [[CB Breogán|Río Breogán]]. It was his first experience in European basketball, taking part in the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[Basketball Champions League]].{{cite web|title=Justin Anderson, físico y calidad para el Río Basket is reinforced with the signing of Justin Anderson |url=https://www.valenciabasket.com/valencia-basket-es-reforca-amb-l39arribada-de-justin-anderson|website=valenciabasket.com|date=December 24, |url=https://www.valenciabasket.com/justin-anderson-leaves-valencia-basket|website=valenciabasket.com|date=July 9, 2024|access-date=June 17, 2025|language=en}} ===FC Barcelona (2024–2025)=== On July 25, 2024, [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] announced Anderson as a new player on a one-season deal through June 30, 2025.{{cite web|title=Justin Anderson joins FC was named Player of the Round for round 14 of the [[2024-25 ACB season]], scoring 25 points in a loss against [[Bàsquet Girona]].{{cite web|title=Justin Anderson, Jugador de la Jornada 14 |url=https://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/491375-justin-anderson-jugador-de-la-jornada-14.html|website=acb.com|date=January 8, 2025|access-date=June 17, 2025|language=es}} On June 17, 2025, Barcelona announced that Anderson would be leaving the team upon his contract's expiry on June 30.{{cite web|title=Justin Anderson's time at Barça ends|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/basketball/first-team/news/4288644/justin-andersons-time-at-barca-ends|website=fcbarcelona.com|date=June 17, 2025|access-date=June 17, 2025|language=en}} === He has an older sister, Eurisha, and an older brother, Edward III, who played basketball for the [[University of Mary Washington]]. ===Community involvement=== Anderson is a member of the "Starting Five", along with [[Malcolm Brogdon]], [[Joe Harris (basketball)|Joe Harris]], [[Anthony Tolliver]], and [[Garrett Temple]]. Their goal was to raise $225,000 through Hoops2O, founded by Brogdon, to fund five wells in East Africa by the end of the [[2018–19 NBA season|2018–19 season]].{{cite news|url=https://waterboys.org/hoops2o/|title=It's Bigger Than Ball: Waterboys Teams Up With The NBA.|work=Waterboys|access-date=February 28, 2019}} Anderson traveled with Brogdon and Harris to [[Tanzania]] to witness the opening of the first well they funded in July 2019, and by November Hoops2O had raised nearly $400,000.{{cite web |last1=Blaustein |first1=Lew |title=Indiana Pacers'
